narrator: Mina Murray (journal), Dr. John Seward (phonograph diary), with letters from Billington & Son, Carter Paterson & Co. and Sister Agatha
summary: After a long walk to Robin Hood's Bay, Mina wakes at 3 a.m. on 11 August to find Lucy gone and runs through Whitby to the East Cliff churchyard, where she glimpses a long dark figure with red gleaming eyes bending over Lucy on their seat; she finds Lucy alone, asleep and gasping, and fastens a shawl at her throat with a safety-pin, leaving two small puncture marks. Over the next days Lucy sleepwalks, sees a bat at the window, murmurs 'His red eyes again' at sunset, and grows pale and weak while two white-edged red marks fail to heal. Mrs. Westenra confides she has weeks to live from her heart. Billington's letters show the fifty earth boxes sent by rail to Carfax, near Purfleet, and delivered to the ruined chapel. Sister Agatha's letter reveals Jonathan survives in a Buda-Pesth hospital with brain fever, and Mina leaves to join him. In Seward's diary Renfield calls out for 'the Master', escapes through his window at night, climbs the wall into Carfax, begs at the ironbound oak chapel door, and is subdued and restrained in a strait-waistcoat in the padded room.

scenes.title: Walk to Robin Hood's Bay
scenes.location: Cliff path, field by the lighthouse, inn at Robin Hood's Bay
scenes.summary: Lucy and Mina are frightened by cows, take tea at a bow-windowed inn over seaweedy rocks, and return exhausted, only to host the curate for supper.
scenes.key_quote: We had a capital 'severe tea' at Robin Hood's Bay in a sweet little old-fashioned inn.

scenes.title: Lucy missing in the night
scenes.location: The Crescent, North Terrace, West Cliff, fish market, bridge
scenes.summary: Mina finds the bed empty, the room door unlocked and the hall door's catch not caught; she takes a heavy shawl and runs through the empty town under a full moon with driving clouds.
scenes.key_quote: The bed was empty. I lit a match and found that she was not in the room.

scenes.title: The dark figure bending over Lucy
scenes.location: West Cliff edge; the steps to the abbey; the churchyard seat
scenes.summary: From the West Cliff Mina sees a white figure on the seat with something dark bending over it; as she climbs the endless steps she cries out and sees a white face with red gleaming eyes. When she enters the churchyard Lucy is alone.
scenes.key_quote: something raised a head, and from where I was I could see a white face and red, gleaming eyes.

scenes.title: Waking Lucy and the safety-pin
scenes.summary: Mina wraps Lucy in the shawl pinned at her throat, puts her shoes on Lucy's feet, wakes her, hides her own muddy feet, evades a drunk man and tucks her in; Lucy begs for secrecy. Mina ties the locked-door key to her wrist.
scenes.key_quote: I have locked the door, and the key is tied to my wrist.

scenes.title: The two little marks
scenes.summary: Two red points on Lucy's throat with a drop of blood on her nightdress; by 17 August the marks are open, larger, with faintly white edges.
scenes.key_quote: They are like little white dots with red centres.

scenes.title: The bat at the window
scenes.summary: Lucy sits up asleep pointing at the window; a great bat circles in the moonlight and flits off toward the abbey.
scenes.key_quote: Between me and the moonlight flitted a great bat, coming and going in great whirling circles.

scenes.title: His red eyes again
scenes.location: Top of the steps from West Pier; East Cliff seat
scenes.summary: Lucy murmurs 'His red eyes again!' as a dark seated figure on their seat seems to have burning eyes, a trick of the sun on St. Mary's windows. That night Mina sees Lucy asleep at the window with a bird-like thing on the sill.
scenes.key_quote: His red eyes again! They are just the same.

scenes.title: Mrs. Westenra's secret
scenes.summary: Arthur's father is better and the wedding is hastened; Mrs. Westenra confides her doctor says her heart will kill her within months.

scenes.title: Lucy fading
scenes.summary: Lucy grows pale and weak, gasping at night, found fainting at the open window despite the key on Mina's wrist.
scenes.key_quote: all the time the roses in her cheeks are fading

scenes.title: The boxes go to Carfax
scenes.location: Whitby solicitors, Great Northern Railway, King's Cross, Carfax chapel
scenes.summary: Fifty boxes are railed to King's Cross and carted to Carfax near Purfleet, placed in the ruined ancient chapel marked 'A', keys left in the main hall; £1 17s. 9d returned.
scenes.key_quote: You will please deposit the boxes, fifty in number, which form the consignment, in the partially ruined building.

scenes.title: Lucy remembers the dream
scenes.summary: Lucy recalls crossing the bridge, dogs howling, something long and dark with red eyes, sweet and bitter scent, sinking into green water, her soul floating above the West Lighthouse.
scenes.key_quote: something long and dark with red eyes, just as we saw in the sunset

scenes.title: News of Jonathan
scenes.summary: Mr. Hawkins forwards Sister Agatha's letter: Jonathan has had six weeks of brain fever, raved of wolves, poison, blood, demons, and arrived on a train from Klausenburg. Mina leaves to join him.
scenes.key_quote: his ravings have been dreadful; of wolves and poison and blood; of ghosts and demons

scenes.title: Renfield speaks of the Master
scenes.summary: Renfield sniffs like a hound, haughty, saying 'the Master is at hand'; then recites a line about bride-maidens.
scenes.key_quote: I don't want to talk to you: you don't count now; the Master is at hand.

scenes.title: Renfield escapes to Carfax
scenes.location: Asylum window, belt of trees, wall, Carfax grounds, chapel door
scenes.summary: Renfield wrenches out his window; Seward follows feet first, sees him scale the wall into Carfax, and finds him pressed against the ironbound oak door of the chapel, begging his Master.
scenes.key_quote: I am here to do Your bidding, Master. I am Your slave, and You will reward me, for I shall be faithful.

scenes.title: Capturing Renfield
scenes.summary: The men close in, Renfield fights like a tiger; he is placed in a strait-waistcoat chained to the wall of the padded room and says 'It is coming'.
scenes.key_quote: I shall be patient, Master. It is coming—coming—coming!

locations.quote: I have taken care that the door is locked and the window securely fastened.

locations.quote: a bright full moon, with heavy black, driving clouds, which threw the whole scene into a fleeting diorama of light and shade

locations.name: East Cliff churchyard seat
locations.description: Favourite seat fixed on a flat stone slab; view over harbour; St. Mary's church and abbey behind.
locations.quote: there, on our favourite seat, the silver light of the moon struck a half-reclining figure, snowy white.

locations.quote: we strolled in the Casino Terrace, and heard some good music by Spohr and Mackenzie

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire feeds on sleepwalking victim from throat
vampire_lore.detail: Two tiny puncture marks, white-edged red centres, do not heal; victim weakens, pale, gasps.
vampire_lore.quote: They are like little white dots with red centres.

vampire_lore.rule: Victim is drawn to the vampire by a trance
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy walks asleep to the churchyard, sits at the window, points at it and remembers a dreamlike drowning feeling.
vampire_lore.quote: I only wanted to be here in this spot—I don't know why, for I was afraid of something.

vampire_lore.detail: Long dark figure with red gleaming eyes; Lucy: 'His red eyes again!'
vampire_lore.quote: His red eyes again! They are just the same.

vampire_lore.detail: Great bat at the window in moonlight, bird-like shape on sill.
vampire_lore.quote: something that looked like a good-sized bird

vampire_lore.detail: Dogs howl all over Whitby as Lucy climbs the steps.
vampire_lore.quote: I heard a lot of dogs howling

vampire_lore.rule: Moves at night under moon and cloud, vanishes in shadow
vampire_lore.detail: Disappears as clouds cover the moon; gone when Mina arrives.
vampire_lore.quote: shadow shut down on light almost immediately

vampire_lore.rule: His earth boxes must be placed in consecrated/ancient chapel soil of Carfax
vampire_lore.detail: Fifty boxes delivered to the ruined chapel of Carfax; Renfield haunts the chapel door.
vampire_lore.quote: the ancient chapel of the mansion

vampire_lore.detail: Renfield becomes haughty, sniffs, announces the Master is at hand, flees to the chapel.

vampire_lore.rule: Victim's blood loss shows as anaemia without anaemic cause
vampire_lore.detail: Mina notes Lucy fades though she eats, sleeps and breathes the fresh air.
vampire_lore.quote: She eats well and sleeps well, and enjoys the fresh air; but all the time the roses in her cheeks are fading

vampire_lore.rule: Marks have dreamy memory of sweet and bitter scent
vampire_lore.detail: Something very sweet and very bitter all around.
vampire_lore.quote: something very sweet and very bitter all around me at once

puzzles.name: Where has Lucy gone?
puzzles.setup: Lucy's bed is empty at night.
puzzles.obstacle: Deduce where a sleepwalker goes from her clothes and the doors.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina notes dressing-gown and dress still in place so she is in nightdress; the hall door catch is unfastened; checks rooms; scans from the West Cliff for the favourite seat.
puzzles.game_idea: Night search puzzle: examine wardrobe, doors and windows for clues to narrow the route, then race the clock across Whitby.
puzzles.quote: Dressing-gown would mean house; dress, outside.

puzzles.name: Shadow run across Whitby
puzzles.setup: Moon and clouds alternately reveal and hide the churchyard.
puzzles.obstacle: Reach the seat before it is too late, via stairs, fish-market and the single bridge.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina flies down the steps to the pier and fish-market, over the bridge and up the endless steps.
puzzles.game_idea: Timed traversal: move only when cloud shadow covers you or when the figure is looking away; stamina bar on the steps.
puzzles.quote: the bridge, which was the only way to reach the East Cliff

puzzles.name: Waking and concealing Lucy
puzzles.setup: Lucy is cold, barefoot and in a nightdress in a churchyard; people may see.
puzzles.book_solution: Shawl, safety-pin, shoes on Lucy, muddy feet for Mina, hide in a doorway from a drunk man.
puzzles.game_idea: Stealth escort: guide Lucy home dodging passers-by, hiding in doorways and wynds.
puzzles.quote: we hid in a door till he had disappeared up an opening

puzzles.name: Securing the sleepwalker
puzzles.setup: Lucy keeps trying the door and window.
puzzles.obstacle: Locked door isn't enough; she goes to the window.
puzzles.book_solution: Key tied to Mina's wrist, window fastened; Lucy still opens it later.
puzzles.game_idea: Room-security puzzle: lock the door, fasten windows, set a watch; discover each lock fails against the vampire's summons until you add wards.
puzzles.quote: I keep the key of our door always fastened to my wrist at night

puzzles.name: Diagnosing the wounds
puzzles.obstacle: Find the true cause rather than the safety-pin.
puzzles.book_solution: Mina attributes them to the pin; unresolved.
puzzles.game_idea: Clue-comparison: match wound spacing and appearance to pin vs bite; choose to call a doctor.
puzzles.quote: the tiny wounds seem not to have healed. They are still open, and, if anything, larger than before

puzzles.name: Catching Renfield
puzzles.setup: Renfield flees out of a window into Carfax.
puzzles.obstacle: A strong lunatic must be tracked, followed over a wall and subdued without scaring him.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward squeezes out feet-first, the attendant watches the direction, a ladder crosses the wall, men surround and overpower him.
puzzles.game_idea: Chase and corner encounter: track his path across the grounds, set men at exits and avoid spooking him before closing the net.
puzzles.quote: Chasing an errant swarm of bees is nothing to following a naked lunatic

puzzles.name: Delivery orders for Carfax
puzzles.setup: Fifty boxes must reach the chapel.
puzzles.book_solution: Train 9:30 p.m., due 4:30 p.m. next day, teams ready, boxes to chapel 'A'.
puzzles.game_idea: Logistics puzzle for the opposing side or an investigator tracking the boxes by paperwork.
puzzles.quote: The goods leave by the train at 9:30 to-night, and will be due at King's Cross at 4:30 to-morrow afternoon.

combat.name: Seizing Renfield at Carfax
combat.tactics: Surround and close in after he is distracted at the chapel door.
combat.outcome: Renfield fights like a tiger but is restrained and chained in the padded room.
combat.game_idea: Party non-lethal capture: encircle positions, use Subdue and Restrain actions; Renfield has high strength and an enrage when approached; each turn the surround tightens.
combat.quote: When we closed in on him he fought like a tiger. He is immensely strong.

combat.name: Dark figure at the seat
combat.tactics: Mina calls out; the figure raises its head and then withdraws.
combat.outcome: The figure disappears; Lucy survives with marks.
combat.game_idea: Pursuit and interrupt scene: shout/light/charge to interrupt a feeding; no kill possible yet, only disrupt.
combat.quote: I called in fright, 'Lucy! Lucy!' and something raised a head

quest_hooks: Night search: find Lucy before the dark figure drains her.
Escort Lucy home unseen and keep her secret.
Guard Lucy's bedroom: lock, window, wards, and watch for the bat.
Examine Lucy's throat: decide whether to call a doctor.
Track the fifty boxes to Carfax and inspect the chapel.
Chase and restrain Renfield before he reaches the chapel.
Travel to Buda-Pesth to rescue Jonathan (Mina's journey).
